name: Dubai
tagline: Desert dunes, record-breaking towers and old-souk soul
description:
Dubai is a city of superlatives — the world's tallest tower, malls with aquariums and ski slopes, islands sculpted into palm trees — yet it rewards travellers who look beyond the glitter. Only a few generations ago this was a modest pearling and trading port, and you can still feel that past along Dubai Creek, where wooden dhows unload cargo, one-dirham abras ferry commuters between souks, and wind-towered houses shade the lanes of Al Fahidi.

Downtown delivers the spectacle: sunset from the Burj Khalifa's observation decks, the dancing fountains, and the calligraphy-wrapped Museum of the Future. Along the coast, Jumeirah's beaches and the sail-shaped Burj Al Arab set the scene for long days in the sun, while the desert beyond the city offers vintage Land Rover drives, falconry and silent starlit dinners.

Visit between November and March, when days are warm rather than scorching. Respect local customs — modest dress away from the beach, discretion during Ramadan — and balance the big-ticket sights with karak chai from a roadside cafeteria, a Friday brunch and a wander through the spice-scented souks of Deira.

safety.notes: Crime is very low and the city feels safe at any hour; the bigger risks are extreme summer heat and strict laws. There is zero tolerance for drugs (check the rules on prescription medicines), public drunkenness and offensive social-media posts.

tipping: Many restaurants add a service charge; if not, 10–15% is appreciated, and rounding up taxi fares or tipping valets and porters AED 5–10 is customary.
gettingAround: The driverless Metro's Red and Green lines (pay with a Nol card) link the airport, Downtown, the Marina and Old Dubai, and taxis and ride-hailing apps are plentiful and affordable; walking long distances is impractical in summer.
tips: Book Burj Khalifa tickets online at least a week ahead for sunset — prime slots cost more but sell out first.
Cross Dubai Creek by traditional abra for a single dirham; it's the most atmospheric ride in the city.
Buy a Nol card at any Metro station, and if you're a man avoid the carriages marked for women and children — fines apply.
In summer, plan outdoor sightseeing for early morning or after sunset, and use air-conditioned malls and Metro walkways to get around.
Friday brunch is a local institution — lavish all-you-can-eat hotel spreads with optional drinks packages — so book popular ones ahead.
Alcohol is served only in licensed venues, mostly inside hotels, so check before booking dinner if you'd like a drink.
etiquette: Dress modestly in malls, souks and Old Dubai by covering shoulders and knees, and save swimwear for beaches and pools.
Public displays of affection beyond holding hands can cause offence and even legal trouble.
During Ramadan, avoid eating, drinking or smoking in public during daylight hours, and keep music low.
Never photograph people, especially Emirati women, without clear permission — privacy laws are strict.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Dubai
neighborhoods.blurb: The city's showpiece around the Burj Khalifa, the Dubai Mall and the fountain lake, packed with luxury hotels and restaurants with skyline views.

neighborhoods.name: Al Fahidi & Bur Dubai
neighborhoods.blurb: Old Dubai on the creek's west bank, where wind-tower houses, the textile souk, temples and cheap Indian eateries sit side by side.

neighborhoods.name: Deira
neighborhoods.blurb: The bustling east bank of the creek, home to the gold, spice and perfume souks, dhow wharves and some of the city's best-value hotels.

neighborhoods.name: Jumeirah
neighborhoods.blurb: A long, low-rise coastal district of villas, public beaches, the Jumeirah Mosque and laid-back cafés, stretching down to the Burj Al Arab.

neighborhoods.name: Dubai Marina
neighborhoods.blurb: A forest of skyscrapers around a man-made marina, with a waterfront promenade, beach clubs and the lively beach walk at JBR.

dishes.name: Machboos
dishes.description: The Emirati national dish: spiced rice cooked with lamb, chicken or fish, dried black lime and baharat — a fragrant cousin of biryani.

dishes.name: Luqaimat
dishes.description: Crisp golden dumplings drizzled with date syrup and sesame seeds, a staple of Ramadan evenings and festive gatherings.

dishes.name: Karak chai
dishes.description: Strong black tea boiled with evaporated milk, sugar and cardamom, sipped from paper cups at roadside cafeterias at all hours.

dishes.name: Shawarma
dishes.description: Spit-roasted chicken or beef shaved into thin flatbread with garlic sauce, pickles and fries — Dubai's favourite late-night snack.

dishes.name: Balaleet
dishes.description: A sweet-and-savoury Emirati breakfast of vermicelli cooked with sugar, saffron and cardamom, topped with a thin omelette.

events.name: Dubai World Cup
events.description: One of the world's richest horse races takes place at Meydan Racecourse, with high fashion, fireworks and a glamorous crowd.

events.name: Art Dubai
events.description: The region's leading contemporary art fair gathers galleries from across the Middle East, Africa and South Asia, with talks and satellite shows around the city.

events.name: Dubai Fitness Challenge
events.description: For 30 days the city gets moving with free workouts and events, including a mass run along a car-free Sheikh Zayed Road past the Burj Khalifa.

events.name: Dubai Shopping Festival
events.description: From December into January, malls and souks offer deep discounts, raffles and nightly fireworks and drone shows across the city.

attractions.name: Burj Khalifa
attractions.description: At 828 metres, the world's tallest building soars above Downtown like a silver needle. High-speed lifts whisk you to observation decks on levels 124 and 125 — or higher for a premium — where the city, desert and Gulf spread out far below.
attractions.bookingTip: Book online well ahead; sunset slots cost more and sell out, while early-morning visits are cheaper and quieter.

attractions.name: Dubai Mall
attractions.description: One of the world's largest malls packs in more than a thousand shops, a vast aquarium tank, an ice rink and a towering dinosaur skeleton. Step outside to the lake at dusk for the Dubai Fountain, whose jets dance to music every half-hour through the evening.
attractions.hours: 10:00–midnight daily; fountain shows every 30 minutes from about 18:00 to 23:00
attractions.bookingTip: Watch the fountain show for free from the lakeside promenade, or from the footbridge to the Souk Al Bahar for a calmer angle.

attractions.name: Museum of the Future
attractions.description: A gleaming stainless-steel ring wrapped in Arabic calligraphy, this museum imagines life decades from now through immersive exhibits on space, ecology and wellbeing. The building itself, glowing at night along Sheikh Zayed Road, is half the attraction.
attractions.bookingTip: Timed tickets often sell out days ahead, so book online as soon as your dates are fixed.

attractions.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
attractions.description: Restored coral-stone and gypsum houses crowned with wind towers line the shaded lanes of Dubai's oldest quarter, now home to small galleries, museums and courtyard cafés. It's the best place to glimpse the city before oil, a short stroll from the creek's abra stations.
attractions.hours: Lanes open 24 hours; galleries and cafés roughly 09:00–20:00
attractions.bookingTip: Come in the cooler morning, then hop on an abra across the creek to the Deira souks.

attractions.name: Dubai Gold Souk
attractions.description: Hundreds of shops glitter beneath a timber-roofed arcade in Deira, their windows stacked with bangles, necklaces and elaborate bridal sets priced by the day's gold rate. Even if you're not buying, the sheer weight of gold on display is a spectacle.
attractions.bookingTip: Pieces are priced by weight at the daily gold rate plus a making charge — haggle on the charge, not the gold.

attractions.name: Burj Al Arab
attractions.description: Rising from its own island like a billowing white sail, this hotel became Dubai's calling card long before the Burj Khalifa. Photograph it from the neighbouring public beach at sunset, or book a guided tour or a meal to see its gold-leafed atrium.
attractions.hours: Exterior viewable any time; interior tours roughly 09:00–19:00 daily
attractions.bookingTip: Viewing from outside is free, but non-guests need a restaurant booking or the official interior tour (around $175) to get past the gate.

attractions.name: Palm Jumeirah
attractions.description: This palm-shaped artificial island is lined with villas, beach clubs and resort hotels along its fronds. Ride the monorail down its trunk, stroll the boardwalk on the outer crescent, or head up to the observation deck at The View for the best look at its shape.
attractions.bookingTip: For the classic aerial view, book The View at The Palm for late afternoon, when the light is warm.

attractions.name: Jumeirah Mosque
attractions.description: One of the few mosques in the UAE that welcomes non-Muslim visitors, this elegant white-stone mosque in medieval Fatimid style hosts guided visits explaining Islamic practice and Emirati culture over dates and Arabic coffee. Questions of any kind are encouraged.
attractions.bookingTip: Check ahead, as visits have been paused at times for renovation; modest dress is required, with robes and headscarves provided.

attractions.name: Jumeirah Beach
attractions.description: A long ribbon of pale sand running south from the old quarter, with public stretches like Kite Beach offering running tracks, food trucks, water sports and a postcard view of the Burj Al Arab. The water is calm, warm and shallow for much of the year.
attractions.hours: Open daily; lifeguards on public beaches roughly 07:00–sunset
attractions.bookingTip: Bring shade and plenty of water, and in the hotter months come early or at sunset — the sand is scorching by midday.

attractions.name: Dubai Desert Conservation Reserve
attractions.description: About an hour from the city, this protected sweep of red dunes shelters Arabian oryx, gazelles and native ghaf trees, and access is limited to a handful of licensed operators. Expect vintage Land Rover drives, falconry and dinners under the stars rather than noisy dune-bashing.
attractions.hours: Operator-led visits at dawn and late afternoon
attractions.bookingTip: There's no independent access — book a licensed conservation safari, which typically includes hotel transfers.

hotels.name: Qasr al-Sahab
hotels.description: A palatial beach resort on the Palm's outer crescent, with butler-serviced suites, a long private beach and an infinity pool facing the Marina skyline. The hammam spa and sunset rooftop lounge are destinations in themselves.

hotels.name: Bait al-Barjeel
hotels.description: Twelve rooms around a courtyard in a restored wind-tower house, with carved teak doors, Persian carpets and a rooftop majlis for sunset Arabic coffee. The abra station is a two-minute walk away.

hotels.name: Falak Design Hotel
hotels.description: Sweeping curves, brushed steel and calligraphy-inspired lighting echo the museum across the road, while rooms gaze down Sheikh Zayed Road's canyon of towers. The rooftop pool bar is a favourite with the after-work crowd.

hotels.name: Sikka Budget Rooms
hotels.description: Clean, compact rooms in a no-frills hotel on a lane behind the Gold Souk, steps from the spice market and the creek. Excellent value, with the Metro five minutes away and cheap Indian and Iranian eateries on every corner.

hotels.name: Mahar Beach Resort
hotels.description: A low-rise, family-focused resort on the Jumeirah shoreline with three pools, a lazy river, a big kids' club and front-row views of the Burj Al Arab. Its beachfront grill and shaded cabanas make it tempting never to leave.

hotels.name: Nujoom Dune Camp
hotels.description: Twenty canvas-and-timber tented suites tucked among red dunes, each with a private stargazing deck and plunge pool. Days start with a sunrise camel walk and end with a fire-pit dinner beneath the Milky Way.

restaurants.name: Shawarma Abu Rashid
restaurants.description: A pavement counter with two spinning spits — chicken and beef — turning out garlicky rolled shawarma that locals and taxi drivers queue for until the early hours. A wrap and a fresh juice cost less than a coffee in Downtown.
restaurants.signatureDish: Chicken shawarma with toum and pickles

restaurants.name: Karak & Chebab House
restaurants.description: A shaded courtyard café serving Emirati breakfasts: saffron chebab pancakes with date syrup and cream cheese, balaleet, eggs with tomato and paper cups of cardamom karak. The perfect fuel before exploring the old quarter.

restaurants.name: Majarra Tasting Room
restaurants.description: A hushed dining room high above Downtown, facing the Burj Khalifa, where a nine-course menu reimagines Gulf and Levantine flavours with caviar, saffron and camel-milk desserts. It's licensed, with an equally inventive zero-proof pairing built on dates, rose and sumac.

restaurants.name: Sufrat Jaddah
restaurants.description: Grandmother-style Emirati dishes served in a converted villa: fragrant machboos, harees slow-cooked for hours and fish saloona with dried lime, finished with warm luqaimat. One of the few places to taste genuine home-style Gulf cooking.

restaurants.name: Udupi Leaf Canteen
restaurants.description: Crisp dosas, fluffy idli and endlessly refilled thalis served on banana leaves in a busy canteen near the textile souk. A full meal costs a few dollars — proof that Dubai can be a budget city too.

restaurants.name: Hamour & Lime Beach Grill
restaurants.description: Toes-in-the-sand tables on Jumeirah's shoreline, where local hamour, prawns and lobster are grilled over charcoal and served with lime, garlic butter and saffron rice. Arrive before sunset for the Burj Al Arab silhouette.

restaurants.name: Arzeh Terrace
restaurants.description: A sprawling sea-view terrace on the Palm serving mezze, charcoal-grilled meats and saj bread baked to order, with shisha under the stars. Weekend family lunches here stretch on for hours.
restaurants.signatureDish: Mixed grill with warm saj bread

restaurants.name: Sumibi Robata Bar
restaurants.description: Sleek counters wrap around a glowing charcoal grill turning out wagyu skewers, miso black cod and grilled corn, with a sake and highball list for the after-work crowd. It's licensed and busiest on weeknights.

experiences.name: Conservation Desert Safari with Falconry and Dune Dinner
experiences.description: Ride through the protected dunes in a vintage open-top Land Rover, watch a falconry display and look out for Arabian oryx and gazelles, then settle into a Bedouin-style camp for a barbecue dinner under the stars. Group sizes are capped to protect the reserve.

experiences.name: Old Dubai Souks and Abra Walk
experiences.description: Start in the Gold Souk, weave through Deira's spice and perfume souks, then cross the creek by abra to the wind-tower lanes of Al Fahidi with a guide who grew up in Old Dubai. There's plenty of time to browse and haggle.

experiences.name: Old Dubai After-Dark Food Trail
experiences.description: Graze across both banks of the creek after sunset, from Emirati luqaimat and Iranian kebabs to Indian chaat and stretchy pistachio-crusted ice cream, crossing by abra between tastings. Come very hungry.

experiences.name: Palm and Burj Al Arab Sunset Yacht Sail
experiences.description: Glide out aboard a sleek yacht, cruising past the Palm's crescent resorts towards the Burj Al Arab as the sun melts into the Gulf. Soft drinks, snacks and a swim stop in the warmer months are included.
